w: The last battleship commissioned by the US Navy, 'Mighty Mo' fought at Iwo Jima and Okinawa before hosting the Japanese Instrument of Surrender on her deck in Tokyo Bay in 1945. Reactivated in 1984 with missile launchers, she later escorted Gulf oil tankers before retiring to Pearl Harbor as a museum ship.
s: The deck where the Second World War officially ended
_facts: Last battleship commissioned by the US Navy, completed 1944
Japanese Instrument of Surrender signed on her deck, Sept 1945
Fought at Iwo Jima, Okinawa, and later the Korean War
Reactivated 1984 with missile launchers, now a museum ship

w: The only royal palace on US soil, this was the residence of Hawaii's rulers from Kamehameha III in 1845 to Queen Liliuokalani, overthrown here in 1893. It then served as capitol for the Provisional Government, Republic, Territory and State of Hawaii until 1969, before reopening as a museum in 1978.
s: America's only royal palace, and site of a coup
_facts: Only royal palace on US soil
Royal residence 1845-1893, Kamehameha III to Liliuokalani
Monarchy overthrown here in 1893
Used as government capitol until 1969; museum since 1978

w: Once called Rabbit Island and site of an ancient Hawaiian fertility ritual banned by missionaries in the 1830s, this islet passed from Kamehameha I to a Spanish deserter, then a sugarcane plantation, before the Navy took it over by 1939. Two years later it sat at the center of the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor.
s: From a fertility rite to the heart of Pearl Harbor
_facts: Formerly Rabbit Island; native name Mokuumeume
Site of an ancient Hawaiian fertility ritual, stopped in the 1830s
Became a sugarcane plantation, then a Navy air/sub station by 1939
At the center of the December 7, 1941 attack on Pearl Harbor

w: Founded in 1922 by Anna Rice Cooke and formally opened in 1927, Hawaii's largest art museum has grown from a private collection into one of the biggest single holdings of Asian and Pan-Pacific art in the United States, now numbering more than 55,000 works.
s: One of America's biggest troves of Pan-Pacific art
_facts: Founded 1922 by Anna Rice Cooke
Officially opened April 8, 1927
Largest art museum in Hawaii
More than 55,000 works, strong Asian/Pan-Pacific holdings

w: Straddling the sunken hull of USS Arizona without touching it, this memorial marks the resting place of 1,102 of the 1,177 sailors and Marines killed aboard her on December 7, 1941. Accessible only by boat, it draws more than two million visitors a year and was declared a National Historic Landmark in 1989.
s: A memorial floating over a sunken battleship's grave
_facts: Marks the resting place of 1,102 of 1,177 killed on USS Arizona
Built 1962, accessible only by boat
Over two million visitors annually
National Historic Landmark since 1989

w: For four decades this 184-foot lighthouse was the tallest structure in Hawaii, greeting arriving ships much as the Statue of Liberty greeted New York's immigrants. Opened September 11, 1926 at Pier 9 in the Hawaiian Gothic style for $160,000, it remains one of the state's most recognized landmarks.
s: Hawaii's tallest building for 40 years, built to say aloha
_facts: Opened September 11, 1926, cost $160,000
Hawaii's tallest structure for four decades
184 ft tall plus 40 ft flag mast, Hawaiian Gothic style
Located at Pier 9 of Honolulu Harbor

w: Founded in 1904 and run by the University of Hawaii since 1919, this is the second-oldest continuously operating public aquarium in the United States, after New York's. Built beside a living coral reef on the Waikiki shoreline, it now holds more than 3,500 organisms across 490 species of marine plants and animals.
s: America's second-oldest aquarium, built beside a reef
_facts: Founded 1904
University of Hawaii institution since 1919
Second-oldest continuously operating public aquarium in the US
More than 3,500 organisms, 490 species

w: One of the first hotels built in Waikiki, the Royal Hawaiian owes its nickname -- the Pink Palace of the Pacific -- to its bright pink stucco facade and Spanish-Moorish towers. Sitting on the beach, it has hosted decades of celebrities and dignitaries as one of Hawaiian tourism's most photographed buildings.
s: The Pink Palace of the Pacific, since Waikiki's early days
_facts: One of the first hotels established in Waikiki
Nicknamed the Pink Palace of the Pacific
Spanish/Moorish-styled architecture, beachfront
Now part of Marriott's Luxury Collection

w: Queen Liliuokalani was arrested in this Greek Revival mansion during the 1893 overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom. It later became the governor of Hawaii's official residence and was named a National Historic Landmark in 2007; a new residence was built behind it in 2008, leaving the original standing as a house museum.
s: Where a queen was arrested as her kingdom fell
_facts: Greek Revival mansion in the Hawaii Capital Historic District
Queen Liliuokalani arrested here during the 1893 overthrow
Later the official residence of Hawaii's governor
National Historic Landmark since 2007; new residence built 2008

w: Once the seat of government for both the Kingdom and the Republic of Hawaii, this building now houses the state's Supreme Court. Its courtyard holds the famous gold-leaf statue of Kamehameha the Great, standing watch as governments rose and fell around him.
s: Kamehameha's gilded statue guards the old seat of power
_facts: Former seat of government of the Kingdom and Republic of Hawaii
Now home to the Hawaii State Supreme Court
Courtyard holds the gold-leaf statue of Kamehameha the Great

w: This extinct volcanic tuff cone above Honolulu holds the National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific, where thousands of American war dead from the Pacific theater are buried within the crater's bowl -- a battlefield's silence traded for a dormant volcano's.
s: War dead resting inside a dormant volcano's crater
_facts: Extinct volcanic tuff cone in Honolulu
